Eastern Cape Farm Abuse - Whipping

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Where do addicts turn when they've burnt all their bridges? Anthony Tovy provides a home and work on his farm in the Eastern Cape. Little did the boys know they'd leave, literally, scarred for life.

Summary:
In the Eastern Cape near Uitenhage lies a farm where Anthony Dovey provides homes for young men that have strayed and are struggling with their addiction to drugs. Anthony offers them a roof over their heads and pays them minimum wage to work on his produce farm. Enter the young addicts: Michael, Adrian, Sam and Matthew. They all lived on the farm. Adrian Pizani has been in every rehab centre in JHB and CT. He has tried many times to get clean, losing his family, friends and young adult years to Herion, Dagga,and Cocaine. He realized his addiction would cost him his life. His best friend Michael Cusdin, who served in the Navy and got hooked on drugs there, told him about the Farm in the Eastern Cape. Little did they know what they were in for. Adrian and Michael spoke to Anthony first on the phone, he said that he has space for them and they decided to leave in early 2014. Anthony, at first, seemed quite normal. The man was in his 40's and the other young men seemed to like him. It wasn't until Adrian and Michael stole a bottle of Anthony's whisky that they found out how Anthony would "cure" them. Anthony tied Adrian to the barn ceiling - called the torture chamber. He handcuffed his hands so he was unable to move, pulled down his pants and made him stand there in his underwear - sometimes Anthony made him go naked. Anthony then took a sjambok and whip and beat Anthony until he would pass out. His scars and injuries were so severe-the photographs speak for themselves. While Anthony inflicted his "torture" on the young man, he got an erection, and screams "suffer, suffer!" All of the young men on the farm were given this same treatment, but Adrian was "special" to Anthony. One night Anthony climbed into bed with Adrian and sexually assaulted him. This caused Adrian to finally leave. Adrian, Michael and Sam are making police cases.

Further information:
In 2013 I received an email from a very distressed young man. He had been beaten badly, but he refused to be interviewed about it, saying he was scared the man - Tony - would kill him. Later, I found out that this was yet another one of Anthony Dovey's victims.

The latest news is that Anthony has two bothers on the farm, an 18 year old and his baby brother who is only 12. They only lasted 2-3 months before coming home.

According to the boys, Anthony Tovy has a terrible temper, and manipulates them. He has done his 'treatment' to many boys and threatens any who want to go to the police. Anthony also says the reason he beats the boys so badly is because he believe that he can "beat addiction" out of them.

So why do these young men not leave? Most are over 18. It's their psychological state, they almost feel they deserve punishment for using drugs. They also have no where else to go. Most feel a beating is better than being out on the street

We are going to do a police raid on wednesday.

Flight down to Eastern cape for confrontation. Vehicle and camera man either from here or up there with presenter.

Re-enactments - pay someone to be the boys - suggestive shots of young man being beaten.

Press Release:


Eastern Cape Abuse
Former drug addicts expose severe physical abuse at an Eastern Cape Farm where they hoped to clean up their act. Carte Blanche investigates a facility set up as a so-called refuge for addicts.
Producer: Sasha Schwendenwein
Presenter: John Webb


Script:


A cattle whip cracks and Alex, not his real name, knows it’s time to be punished. His crime? His addiction to drugs.

ALEX “He then proceeded to handcuff my hand back with my stomach now facing him. It was almost as if I was in a crucifix position. This was extremely terrifying as I could see the whip now, and from a distance he would draw it back. The noise of the whip going through the air before it hits you. He said suffer. That was his word, suffer."

The man wielding the whip is Anthony Michael Dovey – known to most as Tony. He inherited this 18th century cattle farm called Wilgerivier located just outside Port Elizabeth. In 2013 he moved here permanently from Johannesburg. For years he said he’s been taking in young addicts to help them overcome their addictions.

TONY “Over the years there’ve been 17/18 boys through my hands and through my house. All of them had a drug problem."

His aim? To get them clean.

TONY “There is no program as such, except a healthy lifestyle, but usually they only come for a year at a time.”

Carte Blanche checked, and not only is Tony’s farm not a registered rehabilitation centre with the Department of Social Development, but Drug Counselor Justin Jansen said what he’s doing is illegal.

COUNSELOR JUSTIN JANSEN “It wasn’t really a treatment program it’s like a forced labour, you come and work, I’ll beat you. There was no treatment program in place. It’s against the law to do stuff like that.”

Justin knew Alex from a previous rehab before he went to Tony’s farm. In September last year Justin received these cell phone photographs. He said he immediately brought Alex back to his facility after his 8 month stay.

JUSTIN JANSEN “I actually started crying, at what I saw, the abuse that had been inflicted upon someone because they have the disease of addiction."

Alex is now 27 years old and has been clean for over 120 days. He’s adjusting to his new life at - 1 2 B Free - a halfway house in Johannesburg. His scars from the beatings at the farm are still visible.

Alex “The final beating, Tony himself said it was the worst that he’d ever hit anybody. He beat me for two hours with the Whip, the Sjambok and the plank. This time he pulled my underwear down to my knees. Which made me feel deeply humiliated. I was so broken, I couldn’t even retaliate."

Alex was 19 years old when his addiction to crystal meth and khat began. His drug habit spiraled out of control and he would do anything to get his fix - including breaking the law and even stealing from his parents’ home.

ALEX “My lowest point was sitting in Boksburg prison for charges that had been made by my own mother.”

Alex got a call from Tony after his mother had heard about his work with young drug addicts.

ALEX “He would bring me back to basics, the simple life, and would pay me to work on the farm… he also mentioned it was going to be a very painful experience.”

Alex shrugged this off as a joke and his mother agreed to drop the charges only if he tried Tony’s program. Tony drove Alex to the farm, where they joined two other young men already in his care. Alex recognized Johnathan, not his real name, from high school. He was 23 and his addiction began as a teenager.

JOHNATHAN “I realized after parties had gone by, where, on weekends, it was a fact of… Let’s go and get drugs.”

On arrival Tony offered both sedatives. Alex refused, but Johnathan felt he couldn't.

JOHNATHAN “Went to the doctor, and he gave me sleeping tablets to knock me out. I slept for like four days.”

Tony “The first part is drying them out, so to speak, and the doctor, the family doctor helps me with that. And once they’re over the withdrawal symptoms then I put them to work.”

LINK JOHN "The problem with Tony’s admission that he gave the young men sleeping pills when they arrived at the farm to get over their withdrawal symptoms, is that he immediately makes himself guilty of a criminal offense, more than that, an expert has told us, it’s very unusual for recovering addicts to use medication at all, and when they are, those medicines are dispensed by properly qualified people."

TONY "Drugs aren't really the problem, most of the time, there is no father figure or no father willing to be a father figure. They all need discipline and a good role model."

Both young men said they were disciplined within their first two weeks.

JOHNATHAN “I remember counting, I had 68 lashes. And I probably got it the least of all the boys. Like stripes all over you, and some of them, they would cross, so it would welt in the middle, and sort of start to bleed.”

ALEX “Remember he’s released me, he’d offered me a hug, and he said in order to discipline somebody you need to love them.”

Johnathan “When you have words for what your weapons are called then you think something’s not right upstairs. Like the sjambok was called the black mamba…and the cricket bat, he would call that SuperSore, and the whip was called airtime.”

Alex and Johnathan recounted how they were severely tortured for drinking a bottle of Tony’s Whiskey.

JOHNATHAN “I heard noises, the screaming...I just saw my friend, tears in his eyes, like red top to toe, and the next minute I was taken in.”

DR. GIADA “The progression is worrying, because it almost feels like he needs a greater increment of physical pain imposed on someone else to be satisfied.”

Psychologist Dr. Giada del Fabbro, said in contrast, real rehabs use positive reinforcement, because addicts often suffer from low self-esteem.

Dr. GIADA "At some level the victims have to feel like they deserve this, they are to blame and all bad and that Anthony must be all good therefore and he must have what’s best for them at heart.”

Both young men said Tony’s punishments weren't just physical, but psychological too.

JOHNATHAN “He’d walk up to you for the handcuffs, and now you think you’re going to be let out. 42.51 he’ll hold the keys up above you and then he would go and put them back in his pocket. And then hit you again."

Between his cries of pain, Alex said Tony would remind him why he was being punished.

ALEX “You wanted to do drugs, is it nice to do drugs?” 54.42 In this very sick monotone."

DR. GIADA “Where there is actually not just an inflection of physical pain and aggression on these boys but there is a sense of having to humiliate them in some way. It’s really looking at the possibility of some kind enjoyment derived from making others suffer which really is the definition of sadism.”

Although Tony’s victims were initially too terrified, Johnathan and Alex have since opened cases with the police.

JOHNATHAN “He hurt me so much, and it’s just that everyday I think why didn’t I do something about it. Like some many people have asked me questions, why didn’t I do something about it. Hurts me, cos I could have done something, but I was just so scared. I just hope he learns a lesson somewhere along the line.”

15-year old, Ryan, not his real name, and his older brother were both addicts, and lived with Tony in Benoni, before moving with him to Wilgerivier. Ryan’s mother expected her eldest to take care of him, but Tony disciplined him the very first night.

RYAN "He said bend. Grab your ankles. And then he hit me 6 on the arse with a cricket bat. Still today the way he used to hit me, and so often it’s literally affected my coccyx. The bone is so sore sometimes I can’t even sit down.”

Ryan’s mother, Judy, whose name’s been changed to protect her son’s identity, said Tony openly admitted disciplining her sons, and that she saw the horrific results.

JUDY “I saw the marks on the back of his legs…I walked through the garage and that’s when I saw the handcuffs welded to the poles.”

Ryan and Johnathan remember an incident where Ryan’s older brother needed a cell phone.

JOHNATHAN “Tony had a phone and he said what are you willing to do for this phone?"

Ryan’s brother offered to pay it off.

Johnathan “He said no let me give you 12 lashes and then you can have the phone."

Eventually Tony broke him down. As the farm is isolated and there is little access to the outside world, the young man relented.

Johnathan “Okay let me just take those 12 lashes to get a phone to have some contact, and he would take them.”

But worse than the pain, are Ryan’s memories of seeing his older brother being tortured.

JOHN QUESTION “As I asked you the questions about the torture chamber, you seemed to clench and you closed your eyes there?"

RYAN "Seeing your brother handcuffed to a steal bar across the room. Pretty much in tears, and a man standing right in front of him beating him. It’s my brother, if I could I’d do anything to protect him. But I’d never be able to overpower tony."

Judy cried when Ryan recounted what happened when she sent her third and youngest son on holiday with Tony by himself. Instead of sending the boy home, Tony took him to the farm where all three of her sons were told to beat each other, while Tony looked on.

RYAN “If I needed a hiding, he would ask my older brother to do it for him, or me, if I had to give my little brother a hiding. And if we didn't, he’d try give us the hiding.”

Judy said she believed Tony was the lesser of two evils.

JOHN QUESTION "Without wanting to judge, because sometimes people are pushed into certain situations, but did you ever ask yourself questions?"

JUDY "I would sit here and cry and think, what are you doing? But at least they’re not on drugs there. They are safe there, not from Tony’s punishments…but they are not on the streets here. I was fooling myself.”

Alex, Johnathan and Ryan all explained that Tony had a dark side, but there was also a softer, what he called, “mother” side to him.

ALEX “Tony believed that the disciplinary side was the father side…The second part of that he believed we also needed a mothers loving touch. So he would often call us to come lie on his bed. When he was just in his boxers and a t-shirt to almost cuddle him. I didn’t like it cos it made me feel uncomfortable.”

TONY “I always say the kids need a bit of love and a bit of discipline and a lot of food, and so it is with the boys.”

Judy recalls getting a call from her 12 year old son during his holiday.

JUDY "He’s said he’s so uncomfortable right now, because Tony is just… always up in his face. And he’s always touching him. He says he can’t handle this and he was crying.”

This was the final straw for Judy, and she immediately brought both Ryan and her youngest son home to live with her. Johnathan and Alex had similar experiences.

Johnathan "He would lift my shirt and say you’ve got such soft skin here, you’ve got soft skin on your stomach. He’d pinch my nipples. He would squeeze the hell out of them it was sore.”

ALEX “When tony was beating me, he had a hard on. That was sick. I had no doubt in my mind, he’s deriving sexual pleasure from it.”

GIADA “I think if there is sexual arousal, during an act of physical domination and aggression and cruelty, so what we’d call sexual sadism.”

Tony “I’m not saying you should break them, but they have to understand nicely, this is how things work here. Like we were raised, no nonsense was tolerated in the house.”

LINK JOHN "None of the young men we spoke to, Alex, Johnathan or Ryan say they received any kind of therapy while on Tony’s farm outside the town of Uitenhage, in fact, for him, it appears to be all about physical pain, and yet all the experts that we’ve canvassed say there is absolutely no way that you can beat an addiction out of anybody."

DR GIADA “It may be that he continues to escalate, in which, we really have a danger of him killing a boy. Whether that is something that would reinforce his behavior or perhaps it would stop it, we can’t say.”

Alex, Johnathan and Ryan spoke of Tony’s fear that someone would find out about his “punishments.”

JOHNATHAN “He’s always been so scared about – what if people find out what I’m doing?”

Johnathan told Tony he was ready to leave the farm and found a family to live with in Johannesburg. But, in messages to Johnathan last week, Tony expressed relief that Johnathan no longer had photos of his beatings.

T: “That’s a relief.”
T: “Can’t be blackmailed.”

He taunted Johnathan with the memory of the whip.

T: “Have you forgotten about airtime already”
J: “How could I forget that?”
T:“Remember the consequences of doing drugs. Just not worth it.”

LINK 2 JOHN "Well the sign says visits by appointment only, and that’s precisely what we tried to do. Having interviewed a number of people there are some serious allegations leveled against Tony Dovey, so we’ve come to his farm in the Eastern Cape to try and get some answers."

We called the number on the gate.

Tony “It’s not a rehabilitation facility. It’s just I try and help kids as far as I can.”

John “Okay well we’ve spoken to a number of those young men, and we were wondering if we can have a conversation with you about that?”

Unfortunately, Tony was away.

Tony “Call me back tomorrow.”

But the next morning, instead of answering our calls, he sent a text message citing he’s been “advised against an interview.” Three days later, Tony was arrested for assault with the intent to do Grievous Bodily Harm. He appeared in Uitenhage magistrate court and was released with a warning. His case was postponed until April for further investigation. Tony said in a text message to us that he denies the accusations and intends pleading not guilty. He also invited Carte Blanche to attend his criminal trial.Alex said his drug rehab program of abstinence from using both drugs and alcohol is helping. He hopes more people will come forward and that Tony Dovey’s farm of horrors will end here.

ALEX “I knew that Tony was a sick man, often I felt he needed help. Yes in an act of addiction you could walk all over me, but now that I’ve got my mind back and my life back, you can’t walk over me. You can’t treat me like an animal. You can’t treat me like a slave, that I am a human being.”

For years he said he’s been taking in young addicts to help them overcome their addictions. TONY “Over the years there’ve been 17/18 boys through my hands and through my house. All of them had a drug problem." His aim? To get them clean. TONY “There is no program as such, except a healthy lifestyle, but usually they only come for a year at a time.” Carte Blanche checked, and not only is Tony’s farm not a registered rehabilitation centre with the Department of Social Development, but Drug Counselor Justin Jansen said what he’s doing is illegal. COUNSELOR JUSTIN JANSEN “It wasn’t really a treatment program it’s like a forced labour, you come and work, I’ll beat you. There was no treatment program in place. It’s against the law to do stuff like that.” Justin knew Alex from a previous rehab before he went to Tony’s farm. In September last year Justin received these cell phone photographs. He said he immediately brought Alex back to his facility after his 8 month stay. JUSTIN JANSEN “I actually started crying, at what I saw, the abuse that had been inflicted upon someone because they have the disease of addiction." Alex is now 27 years old and has been clean for over 120 days. He’s adjusting to his new life at - 1 2 B Free - a halfway house in Johannesburg. His scars from the beatings at the farm are still visible. Alex “The final beating, Tony himself said it was the worst that he’d ever hit anybody. He beat me for two hours with the Whip, the Sjambok and the plank. This time he pulled my underwear down to my knees. Which made me feel deeply humiliated. I was so broken, I couldn’t even retaliate." Alex was 19 years old when his addiction to crystal meth and khat began. His drug habit spiraled out of control and he would do anything to get his fix - including breaking the law and even stealing from his parents’ home. ALEX “My lowest point was sitting in Boksburg prison for charges that had been made by my own mother.” Alex got a call from Tony after his mother had heard about his work with young drug addicts. ALEX “He would bring me back to basics, the simple life, and would pay me to work on the farm… he also mentioned it was going to be a very painful experience.” Alex shrugged this off as a joke and his mother agreed to drop the charges only if he tried Tony’s program. Tony drove Alex to the farm, where they joined two other young men already in his care. Alex recognized Johnathan, not his real name, from high school. He was 23 and his addiction began as a teenager. JOHNATHAN “I realized after parties had gone by, where, on weekends, it was a fact of… Let’s go and get drugs.” On arrival Tony offered both sedatives. Alex refused, but Johnathan felt he couldn't. JOHNATHAN “Went to the doctor, and he gave me sleeping tablets to knock me out. I slept for like four days.” Tony “The first part is drying them out, so to speak, and the doctor, the family doctor helps me with that. And once they’re over the withdrawal symptoms then I put them to work.” LINK JOHN "The problem with Tony’s admission that he gave the young men sleeping pills when they arrived at the farm to get over their withdrawal symptoms, is that he immediately makes himself guilty of a criminal offense, more than that, an expert has told us, it’s very unusual for recovering addicts to use medication at all, and when they are, those medicines are dispensed by properly qualified people." TONY "Drugs aren't really the problem, most of the time, there is no father figure or no father willing to be a father figure. They all need discipline and a good role model." Both young men said they were disciplined within their first two weeks. JOHNATHAN “I remember counting, I had 68 lashes. And I probably got it the least of all the boys. Like stripes all over you, and some of them, they would cross, so it would welt in the middle, and sort of start to bleed.” ALEX “Remember he’s released me, he’d offered me a hug, and he said in order to discipline somebody you need to love them.” Johnathan “When you have words for what your weapons are called then you think something’s not right upstairs. Like the sjambok was called the black mamba…and the cricket bat, he would call that SuperSore, and the whip was called airtime.” Alex and Johnathan recounted how they were severely tortured for drinking a bottle of Tony’s Whiskey. JOHNATHAN “I heard noises, the screaming...I just saw my friend, tears in his eyes, like red top to toe, and the next minute I was taken in.” DR. GIADA “The progression is worrying, because it almost feels like he needs a greater increment of physical pain imposed on someone else to be satisfied.” Psychologist Dr. Giada del Fabbro, said in contrast, real rehabs use positive reinforcement, because addicts often suffer from low self-esteem. Dr. GIADA "At some level the victims have to feel like they deserve this, they are to blame and all bad and that Anthony must be all good therefore and he must have what’s best for them at heart.” Both young men said Tony’s punishments weren't just physical, but psychological too. JOHNATHAN “He’d walk up to you for the handcuffs, and now you think you’re going to be let out. 42.51 he’ll hold the keys up above you and then he would go and put them back in his pocket. And then hit you again." Between his cries of pain, Alex said Tony would remind him why he was being punished. ALEX “You wanted to do drugs, is it nice to do drugs?” 54.42 In this very sick monotone." DR. GIADA “Where there is actually not just an inflection of physical pain and aggression on these boys but there is a sense of having to humiliate them in some way. It’s really looking at the possibility of some kind enjoyment derived from making others suffer which really is the definition of sadism.” Although Tony’s victims were initially too terrified, Johnathan and Alex have since opened cases with the police. JOHNATHAN “He hurt me so much, and it’s just that everyday I think why didn’t I do something about it. Like some many people have asked me questions, why didn’t I do something about it. Hurts me, cos I could have done something, but I was just so scared. I just hope he learns a lesson somewhere along the line.” 15-year old, Ryan, not his real name, and his older brother were both addicts, and lived with Tony in Benoni, before moving with him to Wilgerivier. Ryan’s mother expected her eldest to take care of him, but Tony disciplined him the very first night. RYAN "He said bend. Grab your ankles. And then he hit me 6 on the arse with a cricket bat. Still today the way he used to hit me, and so often it’s literally affected my coccyx. The bone is so sore sometimes I can’t even sit down.” Ryan’s mother, Judy, whose name’s been changed to protect her son’s identity, said Tony openly admitted disciplining her sons, and that she saw the horrific results. JUDY “I saw the marks on the back of his legs…I walked through the garage and that’s when I saw the handcuffs welded to the poles.” Ryan and Johnathan remember an incident where Ryan’s older brother needed a cell phone. JOHNATHAN “Tony had a phone and he said what are you willing to do for this phone?" Ryan’s brother offered to pay it off. Johnathan “He said no let me give you 12 lashes and then you can have the phone." Eventually Tony broke him down. As the farm is isolated and there is little access to the outside world, the young man relented. Johnathan “Okay let me just take those 12 lashes to get a phone to have some contact, and he would take them.” But worse than the pain, are Ryan’s memories of seeing his older brother being tortured. JOHN QUESTION “As I asked you the questions about the torture chamber, you seemed to clench and you closed your eyes there?" RYAN "Seeing your brother handcuffed to a steal bar across the room. Pretty much in tears, and a man standing right in front of him beating him. It’s my brother, if I could I’d do anything to protect him. But I’d never be able to overpower tony." Judy cried when Ryan recounted what happened when she sent her third and youngest son on holiday with Tony by himself. Instead of sending the boy home, Tony took him to the farm where all three of her sons were told to beat each other, while Tony looked on. RYAN “If I needed a hiding, he would ask my older brother to do it for him, or me, if I had to give my little brother a hiding. And if we didn't, he’d try give us the hiding.” Judy said she believed Tony was the lesser of two evils. JOHN QUESTION "Without wanting to judge, because sometimes people are pushed into certain situations, but did you ever ask yourself questions?" JUDY "I would sit here and cry and think, what are you doing? But at least they’re not on drugs there. They are safe there, not from Tony’s punishments…but they are not on the streets here. I was fooling myself.” Alex, Johnathan and Ryan all explained that Tony had a dark side, but there was also a softer, what he called, “mother” side to him. ALEX “Tony believed that the disciplinary side was the father side…The second part of that he believed we also needed a mothers loving touch. So he would often call us to come lie on his bed. When he was just in his boxers and a t-shirt to almost cuddle him. I didn’t like it cos it made me feel uncomfortable.” TONY “I always say the kids need a bit of love and a bit of discipline and a lot of food, and so it is with the boys.” Judy recalls getting a call from her 12 year old son during his holiday. JUDY "He’s said he’s so uncomfortable right now, because Tony is just… always up in his face. And he’s always touching him. He says he can’t handle this and he was crying.” This was the final straw for Judy, and she immediately brought both Ryan and her youngest son home to live with her. Johnathan and Alex had similar experiences. Johnathan "He would lift my shirt and say you’ve got such soft skin here, you’ve got soft skin on your stomach. He’d pinch my nipples. He would squeeze the hell out of them it was sore.” ALEX “When tony was beating me, he had a hard on. That was sick. I had no doubt in my mind, he’s deriving sexual pleasure from it.” GIADA “I think if there is sexual arousal, during an act of physical domination and aggression and cruelty, so what we’d call sexual sadism.” Tony “I’m not saying you should break them, but they have to understand nicely, this is how things work here. Like we were raised, no nonsense was tolerated in the house.” LINK JOHN "None of the young men we spoke to, Alex, Johnathan or Ryan say they received any kind of therapy while on Tony’s farm outside the town of Uitenhage, in fact, for him, it appears to be all about physical pain, and yet all the experts that we’ve canvassed say there is absolutely no way that you can beat an addiction out of anybody." DR GIADA “It may be that he continues to escalate, in which, we really have a danger of him killing a boy. Whether that is something that would reinforce his behavior or perhaps it would stop it, we can’t say.” Alex, Johnathan and Ryan spoke of Tony’s fear that someone would find out about his “punishments.” JOHNATHAN “He’s always been so scared about – what if people find out what I’m doing?” Johnathan told Tony he was ready to leave the farm and found a family to live with in Johannesburg. But, in messages to Johnathan last week, Tony expressed relief that Johnathan no longer had photos of his beatings. T: “That’s a relief.” T: “Can’t be blackmailed.” He taunted Johnathan with the memory of the whip. T: “Have you forgotten about airtime already” J: “How could I forget that?” T:“Remember the consequences of doing drugs. Just not worth it.” LINK 2 JOHN "Well the sign says visits by appointment only, and that’s precisely what we tried to do. Having interviewed a number of people there are some serious allegations leveled against Tony Dovey, so we’ve come to his farm in the Eastern Cape to try and get some answers." We called the number on the gate. Tony “It’s not a rehabilitation facility. It’s just I try and help kids as far as I can.” John “Okay well we’ve spoken to a number of those young men, and we were wondering if we can have a conversation with you about that?” Unfortunately, Tony was away. Tony “Call me back tomorrow.” But the next morning, instead of answering our calls, he sent a text message citing he’s been “advised against an interview.” Three days later, Tony was arrested for assault with the intent to do Grievous Bodily Harm. He appeared in Uitenhage magistrate court and was released with a warning. His case was postponed until April for further investigation. Tony said in a text message to us that he denies the accusations and intends pleading not guilty. He also invited Carte Blanche to attend his criminal trial.Alex said his drug rehab program of abstinence from using both drugs and alcohol is helping. He hopes more people will come forward and that Tony Dovey’s farm of horrors will end here. ALEX “I knew that Tony was a sick man, often I felt he needed help. Yes in an act of addiction you could walk all over me, but now that I’ve got my mind back and my life back, you can’t walk over me. You can’t treat me like an animal. You can’t treat me like a slave, that I am a human being.” Invoicing Back references from Insert ID in Invoice: Title Author Last Updated Invoice for Eastern Cape Farm Abuse - Whipping (4467 ) Sasha Schwendenwein 02 February 2015

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Where do addicts turn when they've burnt all their bridges? Anthony Tovy provides a home and work on his farm in the Eastern Cape. Little did the boys know they'd leave, literally, scarred for life.
metadata.Summary: In the Eastern Cape near Uitenhage lies a farm where Anthony Dovey provides homes for young men that have strayed and are struggling with their addiction to drugs. Anthony offers them a roof over their heads and pays them minimum wage to work on his produce farm. Enter the young addicts: Michael, Adrian, Sam and Matthew. They all lived on the farm. Adrian Pizani has been in every rehab centre in JHB and CT. He has tried many times to get clean, losing his family, friends and young adult years to Herion, Dagga,and Cocaine. He realized his addiction would cost him his life. His best friend Michael Cusdin, who served in the Navy and got hooked on drugs there, told him about the Farm in the Eastern Cape. Little did they know what they were in for. Adrian and Michael spoke to Anthony first on the phone, he said that he has space for them and they decided to leave in early 2014. Anthony, at first, seemed quite normal. The man was in his 40's and the other young men seemed to like him. It wasn't until Adrian and Michael stole a bottle of Anthony's whisky that they found out how Anthony would "cure" them. Anthony tied Adrian to the barn ceiling - called the torture chamber. He handcuffed his hands so he was unable to move, pulled down his pants and made him stand there in his underwear - sometimes Anthony made him go naked. Anthony then took a sjambok and whip and beat Anthony until he would pass out. His scars and injuries were so severe-the photographs speak for themselves. While Anthony inflicted his "torture" on the young man, he got an erection, and screams "suffer, suffer!" All of the young men on the farm were given this same treatment, but Adrian was "special" to Anthony. One night Anthony climbed into bed with Adrian and sexually assaulted him. This caused Adrian to finally leave. Adrian, Michael and Sam are making police cases.
metadata.Further information: In 2013 I received an email from a very distressed young man. He had been beaten badly, but he refused to be interviewed about it, saying he was scared the man - Tony - would kill him. Later, I found out that this was yet another one of Anthony Dovey's victims. The latest news is that Anthony has two bothers on the farm, an 18 year old and his baby brother who is only 12. They only lasted 2-3 months before coming home. According to the boys, Anthony Tovy has a terrible temper, and manipulates them. He has done his 'treatment' to many boys and threatens any who want to go to the police. Anthony also says the reason he beats the boys so badly is because he believe that he can "beat addiction" out of them. So why do these young men not leave? Most are over 18. It's their psychological state, they almost feel they deserve punishment for using drugs. They also have no where else to go. Most feel a beating is better than being out on the street We are going to do a police raid on wednesday.
